dish: Kurama-yama shōjin zen — temple vegetarian dishes served in red lacquered bowls
address: Kurama, Sakyō-ku, Kyoto (halfway up the steps to Kurama-dera's main gate)
w: Shōjin-ryōri in an old farmhouse with an irori hearth, on the steps up to Kurama-dera. Inside Kyoto calls it the nicest place to eat in Kurama.

dish: Summer kawadoko kaiseki: salt-grilled ayu and amago tempura
w: Inn and restaurant founded in 1932 beside Kifune Shrine. It is one of Kibune's best-known kawadoko spots, serving meals on platforms over the river in summer and a momiji kaiseki out of season.

dish: Kyō-kaiseki of river fish kept live in Kibune spring water; hamo and yuba on the kawadoko
w: Inn and restaurant open since 1962. From May to September it serves kaiseki on river platforms, using river fish that are rested for 2–3 days in mountain spring water before cooking. The casual offshoot Sagenta reopened in 2024.

dish: Kaiseki and sukiyaki served on platforms over the Kibune river in summer
w: A friendly, scenic Kibune riverside restaurant that serves meals on platforms over the Kibune-gawa in the hot months.

dish: Tofu kaiseki of Saga tofu, overlooking the Ōi river
address: Arashiyama, Ukyō-ku, Kyoto (upstream of Togetsukyō Bridge)
w: Seasonal tofu kaiseki in the former holiday villa of Prime Minister Fumimaro Konoe, with views over the Ōi river gorge.

dish: Kikisake tasting set: 18 Fushimi sake poured at a 23 m counter
n: Fushimi Sakagura Kōji (伏見酒蔵小路)
w: An alley of eateries in the sake district with sake from 18 Fushimi breweries (about 120 labels) and food stalls to go with it, from oden to okonomiyaki.

dish: Three-sake flights of Fushimi jizake, chosen daily
n: Ginjō Shubō Abura-chō (吟醸酒房 油長)
address: Ōtesuji shōtengai, Fushimi-ku, Kyoto (4 min walk from Fushimi-Momoyama Station)
w: A sake shop on Ōtesuji arcade that stocks 80+ labels, most of Fushimi's local brews among them. The tasting counter at the back pours flights with snacks.

dish: Ultra-thick kotteri broth that clings to the noodles — the chain's original bowl
n: Tenkaippin Sōhonten (天下一品 総本店)
address: Sakyō-ku, Kyoto (Ichijōji ramen district; ~15 min walk from Ichijōji Station)
w: The original shop of the nationwide kotteri chain, often credited with starting Ichijōji's ramen boom. Fans hold that the broth is still best here.

dish: Mitarashi dango: five small rice dumplings on a skewer in a sweet soy glaze
n: Kamo Mitarashi Chaya (加茂みたらし茶屋), Shimogamo
address: Shimogamo, Sakyō-ku, Kyoto (by the gate of Shimogamo Shrine)
w: A teahouse founded in 1922 outside Shimogamo Shrine, widely called the birthplace of mitarashi dango. The dumplings imitate the bubbles rising in the shrine's Mitarashi pond, and the shop is said to have created the sweet-soy glaze.

dish: Handmade Kyoto udon
address: Okazaki, Sakyō-ku, Kyoto (near Heian Jingū and the Kyoto City KYOCERA Museum of Art)
w: An udon shop with queues every day since it opened in 2006, in the former home of the chef's grandmother near Heian Jingū. It has been recognised by international food guides.

dish: Omurice under a beefy demi-glace; hamburg steak and ebi-fry lunch sets
w: A yōshoku (Western-style) grill in the Heian Jingū/Okazaki area since 1961, best known for its demi-glace omurice.

dish: Teoke bentō: four seasonal Kyō-yasai dishes packed in a wooden hand-pail
w: A Kyoto ryōri house founded in 1899, known for its teoke bentō served in a wooden hand-pail, and for celebration meals such as okuizome and shichi-go-san.

dish: Blend coffee, mixed sandwiches and curry-rice sets at lacquer-craftsman tables
n: Shinshindō Kyōdai Kitamonmae (進々堂 京大北門前)
w: A Paris-style café opened in 1930 at Kyoto University's north gate, nicknamed the university's "second library". Its heavy tables are by lacquer artist Tatsuaki Kuroda.

dish: Inari-zushi with hemp seeds and sesame; the 'nene-una' set of inari, futomaki, saba-zushi, soba and eel; grilled sparrow and quail
address: Fukakusa, Fushimi-ku, Kyoto (by the torii at the back approach to Fushimi Inari Taisha)
w: A Fushimi Inari eatery open since 1540; the name is said to have come from Toyotomi Hideyoshi. Its inari-zushi is the shrine's own dish, and it also sells grilled sparrow and quail skewers to go.

dish: Arashiyama's two sakura-mochi: one wrapped in a salted cherry leaf, one of sticky rice around koshi-an
n: Honke Sakura-mochi Kotokiki Chaya (琴きき茶屋), Arashiyama
address: Saga-Tenryūji, Ukyō-ku, Kyoto (north end of Togetsukyō Bridge)
w: A sweet shop more than 100 years old at the north end of Togetsukyō, whose two kinds of sakura-mochi are an Arashiyama speciality.

dish: Oyakodon with a fluffy half-set egg in sweet dashi; nishin soba with herring simmered a full day
address: Shimogawara-dōri, Higashiyama-ku, Kyoto (about 10 min walk from Gion-Shijō Station)
w: A long-running noodle-and-donburi shop on Shimogawara-dōri near Kōdai-ji, where locals queue at lunch for the oyakodon.

dish: Curry udon
address: Gion, Higashiyama-ku, Kyoto (short walk from Gion-Shijō Station)
w: A low-key Gion udon shop popular with geiko and maiko. It is known for its curry udon and stays open until 2–3 a.m., so it is a usual stop after a night out.

dish: Awa-mochi: millet mochi pounded to order, one piece with koshi-an and one with kinako; eat it the same day
address: In front of Kitano Tenmangū, Kamigyō-ku, Kyoto
w: A wagashi shop facing Kitano Tenmangū with roughly 340 years of history. Its additive-free millet mochi is made only when ordered and keeps for one day. It is on Tabelog's 2023 Hyakumeiten sweets list.

dish: Nama-yuba don and the 'Toyouke-don' of tofu simmered sweet-savoury
n: Toyouke Chaya (とようけ茶屋), Kitano
address: In front of Kitano Tenmangū, Kamigyō-ku, Kyoto
w: The tofu restaurant of Toyoukeya Yamamoto, a tofu maker founded in 1897 opposite Kitano Tenmangū, which opened the restaurant in 1992 to serve its tofu fresh. Lunch only.

dish: Warabi-mochi kneaded by hand every morning; warabi-mochi parfait
address: Shinbashi-dōri, Gion, Higashiyama-ku, Kyoto (beside the Shirakawa canal)
w: A sweets parlour in a former Gion teahouse on the Shirakawa canal. It makes its warabi-mochi by hand each morning and uses Tokachi Dainagon azuki and Yoshino kuzu.

dish: Saba sugata-zushi: whole Sea of Japan mackerel pressed on rice
w: A Kyō-zushi shop opposite Yasaka Shrine, founded in the late Meiji era by a former craftsman of Izuu who was given leave to open his own shop. Its saba-zushi uses true mackerel from the Sea of Japan.

dish: About 80 original breads from a Coupe du Monde de la Boulangerie prize-winner
w: A bakery that draws bread fans from across Japan; owner-baker Jun Tamaki has taken top prizes at the Coupe du Monde de la Boulangerie. Closed Monday to Wednesday.

dish: Uji matcha cuisine: kaiseki courses cooked with matcha
n: Kyō-Uji Matcha Ryōri Tatsumiya (辰巳屋), Uji
w: Founded around 1840 as a tea merchant, this Uji house became a restaurant in 1912 and has cooked with Uji matcha for over a century.

dish: Tango barazushi: the region's layered sweet-mackerel festival sushi
w: A Japanese restaurant open for more than 80 years and known for barazushi, the local dish of the Tango region.

dish: Saga tofu — soft, silky, handmade with groundwater
n: Saga Tofu Morika (嵯峨豆腐 森嘉)
w: A tofu maker dating from the Ansei era (1850s) whose soft, smooth Saga tofu shaped Kyoto's idea of tofu. It appears in Kawabata Yasunari's novel Koto, and Arashiyama yudofu restaurants use its tofu.

dish: Natsukantō: summer-orange jelly set in the hollowed fruit (seasonal); tea-ceremony sweets
w: Arashiyama branch of a Kyoto tea-ceremony confectioner, with a tearoom serving seasonal sweets and, in summer, natural-ice kakigōri.

dish: Sake and otsumami at a classic Kyoto taishū-sakaba
w: A popular sakaba (drinking hall) opened in 1934 near Nishijin. Serai calls it the shrine of Kyoto's taishū-sakaba.
